note: Reference data compiled 2026-10 from operator and agency public information. Routes are simplified (a few waypoints, not survey lines); capacities are nameplate and rounded. Status is as known in mid-2026; check the operator before relying on it.

pipelines.name: Druzhba
pipelines.note: Northern leg to Germany and Poland stopped taking Russian crude in 2023; southern leg to Hungary and Slovakia still runs and has been hit by strikes.

pipelines.name: ESPO
pipelines.note: East Siberia to the Pacific port of Kozmino, with a branch to Daqing in China.

pipelines.name: Keystone
pipelines.note: Alberta oil sands to the Midwest and the Gulf Coast.

pipelines.name: Trans Mountain
pipelines.note: Edmonton to the Pacific at Burnaby; the 2024 expansion tripled capacity and opened Asian markets for Canadian crude.

pipelines.name: Enbridge Mainline
pipelines.note: Largest crude system into the US Midwest; Line 5 crosses the Straits of Mackinac to Sarnia.

pipelines.name: Dakota Access
pipelines.note: Bakken shale in North Dakota to the Patoka hub in Illinois.

pipelines.name: Permian to Corpus Christi
pipelines.note: Several lines (Cactus II, Gray Oak, EPIC and others) take Permian crude to the main US export port.

pipelines.name: Trans-Alaska (TAPS)
pipelines.note: Prudhoe Bay to the tanker port at Valdez.

pipelines.name: BTC
pipelines.note: Caspian crude from Baku via Georgia to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

pipelines.name: Kirkuk–Ceyhan
pipelines.note: Iraqi and Kurdish crude to Ceyhan; stopped in March 2023, restarted in late September 2025 at limited volumes.

pipelines.name: East–West (Petroline)
pipelines.note: Saudi crude from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea: the main way around the Strait of Hormuz.

pipelines.name: Habshan–Fujairah (ADCOP)
pipelines.note: UAE crude to Fujairah, outside the Strait of Hormuz.

pipelines.name: SUMED
pipelines.note: Red Sea (Ain Sukhna) to the Mediterranean (Sidi Kerir); used when tankers are too large for the Suez Canal.

pipelines.name: CPC
pipelines.note: Kazakh crude from Tengiz to Novorossiysk on the Black Sea; the terminal has been hit by drones.

pipelines.name: EACOP
pipelines.note: Ugandan crude to the Tanzanian port of Tanga.

pipelines.name: Myanmar–China
pipelines.note: Bay of Bengal to Kunming: lets China land some Middle East crude without passing Malacca.

pipelines.name: Colonial
pipelines.note: Gasoline, diesel and jet from the Gulf Coast to the US East Coast; a 2021 ransomware attack shut it for six days.

pipelines.name: Nord Stream 1 and 2
pipelines.note: Russia to Germany under the Baltic. Three of four strings were destroyed in September 2022; no gas flows.

pipelines.name: Yamal–Europe
pipelines.note: Russia via Belarus to Poland and Germany; Russian flows stopped in 2022.

pipelines.name: Ukraine transit (Brotherhood)
pipelines.note: Russian gas transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025 when the transit contract expired.

pipelines.name: TurkStream
pipelines.note: Russia to Turkey under the Black Sea, one string continuing to Bulgaria, Serbia and Hungary: the last pipeline route for Russian gas into the EU.

pipelines.name: Southern Gas Corridor (TANAP + TAP)
pipelines.note: Azerbaijani gas through Georgia and Turkey to Greece, Albania and Italy.

pipelines.name: Power of Siberia
pipelines.note: East Siberian gas to northeast China.

pipelines.name: Power of Siberia 2
pipelines.note: West Siberian gas via Mongolia to China; a binding memorandum was signed in September 2025, price terms were still open.

pipelines.name: Central Asia–China
pipelines.note: Turkmen gas through Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan to Xinjiang.

pipelines.name: Transmed
pipelines.note: Algerian gas through Tunisia and Sicily to mainland Italy.

pipelines.name: Medgaz
pipelines.note: Algeria to Almería in Spain.

pipelines.name: Greenstream
pipelines.note: Libya to Gela in Sicily.

pipelines.name: Langeled
pipelines.note: Norwegian gas to Easington, the UK's largest single supply.

pipelines.name: Baltic Pipe
pipelines.note: Norwegian gas via Denmark to Poland, opened in 2022.
